summary: Affinity lease renewal lag triggers mixed routing and unintended fallback during gradual canary rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightMap Analytics, dedicated tenant) reported seeing mixed model outputs and a sudden spike in fallback routing to the canary variant during a slow, weighted rollout. Tenant had a model version pinned for a subset of sessions; several of those sessions received responses from the new canary variant for short windows (~10-30s) before affinity restored. Impact: inconsistent inference outputs, user-visible quality regressions for affected sessions, and a brief increase in token costs due to replayed requests.

Impact:
- ~120 sessions observed mixed routing over a 24-minute window (2026-03-13 02:08–02:32 UTC).
- Customer reports downstream quality alerts and a rollback request.
- No full outage; requests completed with increased latencies and occasional 5xx spikes correlated with the event.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east-1) - dedicated capacity pool: dp-09b4
- Edge tier: edge-v3-proxy cluster (ASG edge-us-east-1-3)
- Canary rollout: weighted rollout 5% -> 25% over 2 hours; affected sessions were meant to remain pinned to stable variant via session affinity (lease TTL 60s).
- Customer pinned version: rw-infer-v2-medium@2026-03-10, canary variant: rw-infer-v2-medium@2026-03-13-canary

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Begin weighted rollout and verify canary weight increasing (5% at 01:50 UTC).
2) Simulate long-running sessions that rely on affinity (session token kept alive).
3) Introduce a synthetic edge-proxy restart/rolling restart (we observed an internal edge-restart job at 02:06 UTC).
4) Within ~2 minutes after the restart, sessions intermittently lost affinity and routed to canary for a single request before re-binding to original pinned variant.

Logs / Observations:
- edge-proxy logs (edge-us-east-1-3) show lease_renewal_rpc latency spikes from ~12ms baseline to 1.2s at 2026-03-13 02:07:34 UTC.
- Router metric `session_affinity_miss` spiked from 0.3/min to 18/min during the window.
- Serving-runtime returned canary variant for requests that carried the original session token; token verification succeeded but affinity lookup returned 404 for a short period.
- No auth/SSO rotation events for the tenant in the timeframe.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Edge-proxy lease renewal requests timed out due to transient RPC backpressure during the rolling restart, causing the affinity store to drop or fail to return binding for a narrow window. Router fallback policy allowed requests without confirmed binding to be routed via the canary path (safe default), resulting in mixed outputs.
Secondary: A TTL/lease-reconciliation race between the canary-controller's cohort rebalancer and the edge's lease-renewal path surfaced because of accelerated canary weight change combined with pod restarts.

Temporary mitigation / Workaround applied:
- Support manually pinned the tenant at the router layer to force stable variant for 30 minutes and initiated a controlled drain of edge-proxy hosts that exhibited high lease latency.
- Canary rollout paused (canary weight set to 0%) and an emergency config was applied to increase affinity lease TTL to 180s for all dedicated tenants.
- Customer notified and asked to hold heavy evaluation traffic for 1 hour.

Next steps / Action items:
1) SRE: Investigate edge-proxy restart job logs and autoscaler activity around 02:05–02:10 UTC (Omar).
2) Runtime: Add additional logging around affinity-store RPC failures to capture call path and error codes (Maya + Helena).
3) Reconciler: Review lease-reconciliation logic for races when pod restarts coincide with weight change events; propose a backoff or hold window (PR referenced).
4) Product: Consider defaulting to rebind-to-stable policy for pinned sessions during rollout windows for dedicated tenants.
5) Follow-up: Run a controlled repro in staging simulating edge rolling restarts + gradual rollout to validate fixes.

Owner: Omar Patel (SRE)
Priority: P1 / Sev1

Attachments / Links:
- Grafana: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/affinity/lease-renewal?orgId=1&from=2026-03-13T02:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T02:40:00Z
- Edge logs (scrubbed): s3://redwood-support-logs/SUP-402321/edge-proxy-us-east-1-3-02-07.gz
- Reconciler PR for investigation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/1427
comments: 2026-03-13 03:12 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage completed. Confirmed routing patterns and correlated with edge restart job. Paused canary and increased TTL as temporary mitigation. Notified customer of workaround and next steps.

2026-03-13 04:05 UTC - Omar Patel (SRE): Investigating edge restart. Early signs point to lease RPC queue saturation on edge-proxy replicas that were being rotated by the patch deployment. Collecting heap/latency traces.

2026-03-13 07:40 UTC - Helena Ruiz (Runtime): Added debug logging branch to affinity client to capture error payloads. Will roll to staging and capture one repro run. Linked GH PR 1427 for code-level notes.
2026-03-14 09:21 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Customer accepted workaround and requested a postmortem and permanent fix timeline. Scheduled a follow-up customer call for 2026-03-15 15:00 UTC.

2026-03-14 12:02 UTC - Omar Patel (SRE): Found correlation with edge autoscaler flapping due to noisy neighbor VMs; adding a mitigation to stabilize ASG scale-in cooldown and applying a hotfix to backpressure lease requests under restart.
resolution_notes: Mitigations: paused canary, increased affinity TTL, forced tenant pin at router. Next steps include autoscaler cooldown tuning and reconciler race fix. Postmortem scheduled and patch PR opened.
